description: AI/ML team hacking on NASA open data. Seeking frontend, design, and domain-science teammates who want to build and win
summary:
• Mission Support. Decades of robotic missions have gathered vast amounts of Martian data, but human explorers will need that information unified in real time.
• Safe Marswalks. The goal is to create a localized, multi-layer map or interface that helps astronauts plan routes, avoid hazards, monitor current conditions, and conduct scientific research during surface excursions.
• Domains. Human Exploration, Mars, Planets & Moons, Software, and Space Exploration.
• Target Users. Astronauts conducting extravehicular activities (EVAs) on the Martian surface and mission planners supporting their operations.
details: Marswalk Planner is a browser-based tool for planning a spacewalk on Mars, set at the boxwork ridges Curiosity studied on Mount Sharp, Gale crater. It has three modes: Plan: The map covers a 1.28 × 0.88 km area at 8 m per grid cell, with up to seven data layers you can switch on and fade: optical, topography with contours, slope hazard, thermal inertia, mineralogy, rock cover and radiation dose. A route finder links the science stops so the walk takes the least time. Its walking-speed model accounts for slope, Mars gravity, loose sand, rocks and the weight being carried. Slopes of 25° or more and dense boulder fields are off-limits. Safety check: A GO / NO-GO status requires at least 25% of suit air and power left on return. It adds up the radiation dose along the route (more where the sky is open, less beside cliffs), flags returns after 4:30 PM local solar time, and a solar storm alert grounds the walk and highlights nearby shelter. Inspect: Tap any point to see its terrain type, slope, thermal inertia, minerals, rock cover, open sky and dose rate, plus a 3D first-person view toward the next stop, so the crew knows what to expect before they go. Visor HUD: Plays the walk through the helmet visor, with a compass strip, markers for each stop, elapsed time, air left, radiation dose, and warnings for steep ground, loose sand, cliffs and low supplies. Benefits: It combines datasets that are normally viewed separately into one local, safety-first view sized for a single walk, which global tools like Mars Trek aren’t designed for. It works for planning inside the habitat, on a tablet in the field, or as a helmet display. Tools: HTML5 Canvas and plain JavaScript (A* route finding, terrain shading, sky-view radiation model, 3D first-person terrain rendering). It runs in any browser with nothing to install. Current limitation: the demo terrain is generated by code to match the setting. Each layer is built to take real NASA maps of the area (HiRISE, THEMIS, CRISM) through a single replace-with-real-data point in the code.
